Assess Fitted Scale Probabilities from an Uncorrected Laplace Fit

Source: R/bayes_laplace_diagnostic.R
diagnose_bayes_laplace.Rd

Check the probability that each fitted scale lies at or below a distance you name, as reported by a joint Laplace or uncorrected marginal Laplace fit, against a fresh importance-weighted estimate of the same posterior. Read this check alongside the fit's own optimizer and integration diagnostics.

Usage

diagnose_bayes_laplace(
  object,
  thresholds,
  scale = c("distance", "log"),
  tolerance = 0.05,
  candidates = 16384L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A fitted multiScale_bayes() object from method = "laplace", or from method = "marginal" without importance correction, with its approximation draws and geometry intact. The check needs the RTMB and posterior (version 1.6.0 or later) packages.

thresholds

Named list of scale thresholds, as in diagnose_bayes_probabilities(). Each name selects a fitted landscape predictor, and each vector holds distinct finite thresholds, such as list(habitat = c(150, 350)). Every threshold is checked for every distinct fitted combination of scale covariates and groups, such as each year.

scale

Units of thresholds. "distance" (default) uses map units and needs positive values. "log" uses natural log map units. The event is a fitted kernel scale less than or equal to the threshold.

tolerance

Absolute difference in probability that matters for your inference, strictly between 0 and 1; default 0.05. Choose it, and the thresholds, before looking at the results.

candidates

Number of fresh importance candidates, at least 2000; default 16384. The validation study used 65536. More candidates can reduce simulation error when the proposal overlaps the posterior well. Every candidate is kept for the weight and event diagnostics, so memory use grows with this number and with the number of parameters.

seed

Optional positive integer seed for the assessment. Your own random-number state is restored afterward.

Value

A list with these elements.

  • available: TRUE when importance ratios and reference summaries could be calculated. A reference that fails its overlap checks is still available, but its statuses stay "unresolved".

  • reason: why the reference is unavailable, why it failed its overlap checks, or that the original fit failed its own diagnostics. An empty string otherwise.

  • raw_diagnostics: the fit's original diagnostics, unchanged.

  • overlap: the importance checks of the reference (passed, pareto_k, ess, min_tail_ess, max_weight, split_cdf_error), or NULL when the reference is unavailable.

  • target_evaluation: counts of posterior density evaluations and of rechecks of invalid values.

  • probabilities: a data frame with one row per fitted scale combination and threshold. covariate, group, row, threshold, and threshold_scale identify the event. approximation is the probability from the fit's draws and reference the importance-weighted probability, with its Monte Carlo standard error reference_mcse. difference is the approximation minus the reference, and difference_lower and difference_upper bound it numerically. indicator_ess is the effective sample size of the reference event indicator, split_reference_difference the absolute difference between the two halves of the reference, and status the verdict described in "Read the status".

  • candidates, seed, tolerance: the settings used.

  • coefficient_proposal: the number of fallback coefficient proposals (fallbacks) and the largest remaining Newton step (max_step).

  • defensive_draws: the number of candidates drawn from the defensive prior component.

  • metadata_establishes_eligibility: always FALSE.

Details

This function is experimental. Its arguments and results may change in a later release without a deprecation period.

Read the status

statusMeaningWhat to do
"discrepancy"The numerical bounds on the difference lie wholly beyond tolerance on one sideDo not report the approximate probability. Sample the model
"within_tolerance"Both bounds lie inside toleranceYou can report the approximate probability, for this threshold only
"unresolved"Every other case, including a reference too imprecise or overlapping the posterior too poorly to decideTreat the probability as unchecked. Raise candidates, or sample

An event can be resolved only when the reference passes the package's importance overlap checks, the original fit passed its own diagnostics, the event has an indicator ESS of at least 400, and the two independent halves of the reference differ by no more than the smaller of 0.05 and tolerance. The bounds combine three standard errors of the weighted reference with Wilson bounds for the original approximate draws. A constant reference indicator also leaves the event unresolved. Expect "unresolved" often, and read it as "not checked", not as "close enough". vignette("v15-bayesian-computation", package = "multiScaleR") reports how often each status occurred in simulations.

How the reference is built

Candidates come 80% from heavy-tailed local proposals around the approximation and 20% from a defensive component based on the latent-effect and scale priors. Response coefficients are drawn from their exact Gaussian conditional, or from a normalized heavy-tailed conditional proposal for other families. The full posterior density and the actual mixture density determine every weight. Neither the approximation nor its draws are replaced.

This exploratory check targets only the requested scale probabilities. A heavy-tailed proposal can still miss posterior regions. The report does not certify approximation accuracy, general calibration, held-out predictions, or the fit's original diagnostics. Compare with a full posterior fit whenever your conclusions depend on these probabilities.

See also

multiScale_bayes(), diagnose_bayes_probabilities(), posterior_scales(), multiScaleR_bayes; vignette("v15-bayesian-computation", package = "multiScaleR").

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("RTMB", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("posterior", quietly = TRUE)) {
  example <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "bayesian-annual-example.rds",
    package = "multiScaleR"))
  # A joint Laplace fit of the annual model, which takes about a second
  fast_fit <- multiScale_bayes(count ~ habitat + factor(year) + (1 | site),
    example$inputs, example$data, scales = list(habitat = ~1 + (1 | year)),
    row_id = "site_year", family = "nbinom2",
    priors = list(scale_median = 250, scale_group_sd = 0.5),
    method = "laplace", seed = 527001)

  # Probability that each year's sigma is 150 m or less. The smallest
  # candidate budget keeps this example short. The validation study used
  # 65536 candidates.
  check <- diagnose_bayes_laplace(fast_fit,
    thresholds = list(habitat = 150), candidates = 2000, seed = 127)
  print(check$reason)   # empty when the reference and the fit passed
  print(check$probabilities[c("group", "approximation", "reference",
                              "status")])
  # "unresolved" means the probability was not checked, not that it is
  # close enough.
}
#> [1] "The reference did not pass the posterior importance overlap checks."
#>       group approximation   reference     status
#> 1 year=2021        0.0140 0.001640765 unresolved
#> 2 year=2022        0.0175 0.002140476 unresolved
#> 3 year=2023        0.2050 0.108813215 unresolved
#> 4 year=2024        0.0175 0.003687778 unresolved
#> 5 year=2025        0.1465 0.002778998 unresolved
# }
